key_decisions.decision: SC-059: Check: a mapped share that answers only after 'Drives' is shown gets its button in letter order (Windows Sandbox, silenced loopback share woken at about 20 s and about 120 s)
key_decisions.rationale: SL-002's validation (ledger validations id 247, two disposable Windows Sandbox runs with a silenced mapped Y:) already measured three of the four parts. Only C:'s button showed (DrivePanel.buttons=1; HEAD 0). DriveStatus left 'Looking for drives...' about 1.9 s in ('drives in held=1909/1911'). WM_CLOSE left the process alive past 120 s on HEAD and the slice alike, and Q-006/U-006 own that. A no-path launch reads drives through the same OnLoaded→LoadDrives path (MainWindow.xaml.cs:149-154), and the network-pass staleness belongs to SC-006, which is why SC-058 was dropped. What is left is a share that answers after 'Drives' getting its button in place (Q-007/U-007). Only DriveReadsTests.cs:76 and :171 prove it, with blocked delegates; the silenced Y: never answered. TAAD can check it in the same Sandbox set-up, which needs no person and changes nothing on this PC (SL-002 critique-1.json:135), so the filer's 'person-run' does not hold.

payload.coherence_check: One direct change, built as the candidate describes it -- with anything bundled into it, which its description lists. A part that no longer holds (already fixed, or misread) is left alone, and the build says so.

cases.behaviour: SC-059: In a Windows Sandbox, map Y: to a loopback share, then silence its server (LanmanServer, srv2 and srvnet stopped; a listener on 445 that never answers). The published exe shows C:'s button and leaves 'Looking for drives...' within about 2 s. Wake the server about 20 s after launch, and in a second run about 120 s after (past the client's ~60 s give-up). In each run Y:'s button must then appear after C:'s: DrivePanel.buttons reads 2, from a report whose ending comes after the wake. A run where Y:'s read ends and no button appears fails the check, and records whether the read returned not-ready or was still blocked.
cases.why: the slice manager named the behaviour a test must pin

direct_change.title: Check: a mapped share that answers only after 'Drives' is shown gets its button in letter order (Windows Sandbox, silenced loopback share woken at about 20 s and about 120 s)
direct_change.description:
A drive that does not answer needs a share that stops answering, which changes this machine's SMB mappings or the person's own server (spike 2's constraints). That is person-run by project rule. The loop proves the same isolation with a blocked delegate in DriveReadsTests.

Put outside SL-002 by its design (#207): only a person can check this, so it is not a criterion any build of that slice could meet.
direct_change.worth: A person who launches the app while a mapped share is asleep is promised that share's button 'whenever it does answer' (MainWindow.xaml.cs:160-164). This PC's Z:\ is a Tailscale peer that goes offline. No late button has ever been seen in the real app. If the woken redirector fails the blocked call instead of finishing it, ReadDrive returns null (MainWindow.xaml.cs:190-202) and the share gets no button until a relaunch. Not seen yet, but ordinary use reaches it: launch while the share sleeps, then it wakes.
